items.title: 60499_Garvin Bushell oral history interview
items.q: We had to borrow money from Old Man Bailey to pay our taxi cab fare to go the railroad station.

ctx.x: Oh, I wouldn't dare go south in those days. I had been south with the circus and that was enough for me. And, what happened was, we - it took all the money that I had and that the four of us had to get the two of us out of jail because we had to pay the policy - Pete and he had to pay the judge, and all that sort of thing. Get us off to keep from doing six months. So we had enough money to get from Chicago to Pittsburgh, the four of us. We didn't have another penny after that. So we went to the hotel where we had…

we didn't have anything to eat, so he fed us. He said, "Look, there's a dance down at Duquesne Garden tonight. Why don't you go down there and play. Maybe you can pass the hat or something." So, the trombone player said, "Let's do that." So that night we went down to Duquesne Garden. We told the leader -- and Old Man Bailey went with us and said what had happened. We got up on the stand and played the Tiger Rag with their rhythm section -- we played the solos and passed the hat. Monk, you're sitting there but…
